compounds 3c and 4a are the first monoterpene-derived compounds that inhibit Tdp1 and that they may be useful as sensitizing agents in combination with topotecan.
2-aminoadamantane derivatives are more potent Tdp1 inhibitors than 1-aminoadamantanes, while the former are less cytotoxic than the latter.

the monoterpene-derived compounds with a nitrogen atom in position 1 of the adamantane ring are the most potent Tdp1 inhibitors and that the compounds with a nitrogen in position 2 are the most cytotoxic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the compounds described in the current study may have potential for development into new drugs for treatment of cancers that are resistant to topoisomerase inhibitors.
the Tdp1 inhibition is a promising strategy to improve the therapeutic efficacy of topotecan and other topoisomerase inhibitors.
the monoterpene-derived fragment of the compounds studied is responsible for their Tdp1 inhibition and that the adamantane fragment is important for the cytotoxicity enhancement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of the monoterpene and adamantane moieties can be successfully used to design potent inhibitors of Tdp1.
aminoadamantane-based compounds containing monoterpene fragments can be developed as Tdp1 inhibitors.
